42	
43	## 1. System Overview & Mental Model
44	
45	deadreckon is a Rust 2024 CLI harness whose default flow is **unattended long-running coding tasks**: `deadreckon run <goal>` creates durable run state, picks a BYOK provider route, executes turns inside a platform-native sandbox, writes spend/provenance/trace records after every turn, and exits only when the LLM declares done, a budget caps the run, or the operator kills it. The CLI is the user-facing layer; `deadreckon-runtime` owns orchestration across providers, sandboxes, docs, and promotion; `deadreckon-core` owns deterministic primitives and durable schemas.
46	
47	```
48	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
49	│ USER                                                                      │
50	│ deadreckon run "make a hello-world Rust binary" --max-spend 5             │
51	└────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
52	                                 │
53	┌────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────┐
54	│ CLI LAYER (crates/deadreckon)                                             │
55	│   cli.rs       clap parser definitions                                    │
56	│   main.rs      command handlers, ratatui rendering, post-run summary       │
57	└────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
58	                                 │ create_run → acquire_lock → runtime loop
59	                                 ▼
60	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
61	│ RUNTIME ORCHESTRATION (crates/deadreckon-runtime)                         │
62	│                                                                           │
63	│  turn_loop.rs  provider turns, sandboxed tool dispatch, cancellation,      │
64	│                acceptance gate invocation, promotion orchestration         │
65	│  polish.rs     optional end-of-run doc polish via a doc-provider           │
66	└──┬──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬────────────────┘
67	   │ durable primitives       │ ProviderRouter::complete  │ run_sandbox
68	   ▼                          ▼                          ▼
69	┌──────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐
70	│ CORE LIBRARY             │  │ PROVIDERS            │  │ SANDBOX              │
71	│ state, paths, locks      │  │ HTTP: anthropic,     │  │ sandbox-exec, bwrap, │
72	│ artifacts, docs, events  │  │ openai, compatible   │  │ docker, none, auto   │
73	│ gate, promotion, chains  │  │ CLI: claude, codex   │  │ policy, PID/cancel   │
74	│ adapter-free schemas     │  │ TEST: smoke          │  │ doctor checks        │
75	└────────────┬─────────────┘  └──────────┬───────────┘  └──────────┬───────────┘
76	             │                           │                         │
77	             └───────────────────────────┴─────────────┬───────────┘
78	                                                       ▼
79	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
80	│ RUNTIME STATE (~/.deadreckon/)                                            │
81	│ runstate/<scope>/runs/<run-id>, library/<scope>/<run-id>, locks, config   │
82	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
83	```
84	
85	Why this shape works:
86	
87	- **The CLI is thin.** It parses args, sets up state, hands off to `deadreckon-runtime`, and prints summaries. Durable schemas and atomic file operations live in `deadreckon-core`.
88	- **State is on disk before every meaningful change.** `state.json` is atomic-written via temp+rename after every phase transition, snapshot, spend record, and tool call.
89	- **The agent cannot mark its own gate.** `dr-gate` is a separate binary that signs an acceptance marker against a nonce only it can read; the deadreckon binary refuses to mark a run `Completed` without that signed marker.
90	- **Sandboxes are platform-native.** macOS uses Seatbelt; Linux uses Bubblewrap; Docker is opt-in. No daemon, no `bollard`, no Lima.
91	- **BYOK extends to subscriptions.** Subscription-bearing users drive deadreckon by routing turns through their local `claude` or `codex` CLIs; no API key required.

95	## 2. Component Map
96	
97	### 2.1 Workspace shape
98	
99	`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/Cargo.toml:1-41`:
100	
101	- Edition `2024`, resolver `3`, workspace version `0.1.0`.
102	- Five workspace members:
103	  - `crates/deadreckon-core` — library for durable state, artifacts, gates, docs, locks, chains, and codebase-mode primitives.
104	  - `crates/deadreckon-runtime` — library for provider/sandbox orchestration, the turn loop, and doc polish.
105	  - `crates/deadreckon-providers` — library for provider config, adapters, and fallback routing.
106	  - `crates/deadreckon-sandbox` — library for platform-native sandbox backends and per-tool policy.
107	  - `crates/deadreckon` — binary (`deadreckon`) + binary (`dr-gate` at `src/bin/dr-gate.rs`).
108	
109	### 2.2 Crate-by-crate
110	
111	**`deadreckon-core` (`crates/deadreckon-core/src/lib.rs`).** Re-exports the public surface of the harness primitives. Modules:
112	
113	| Module | Purpose |
114	|---|---|
115	| `state.rs` | `PipelineState`, `RunStatus`, `PhaseId`, `PhaseState`, `create_run`, `load_run`, atomic writes |
116	| `paths.rs` | `DeadreckonPaths`, `workspace_scope`, `task_key`, all path resolution |
117	| `lock.rs` | `LockState`, file locks via `fs2`, PID liveness via `nix::kill(pid, 0)`, heartbeat |
118	| `promotion.rs` | `promote_completed_run`, manifest writing, atomic working→library swap, crash recovery |
119	| `gate.rs` | `AcceptanceMarker`, signature validation, anti-self-attestation |
120	| `artifacts.rs` | `copy_tree`, `snapshot_working`, `append_{spend,trace,provenance}` |
121	| `cancel.rs` | cancellation markers and run-root cancel checks |
122	| `chain.rs` | autonomous goal-chain records and conductor state |
123	| `codebase.rs` | worktree/copy/fresh/in-place mode records and source materialization |
124	| `docs.rs` | deterministic run-doc templates, frontmatter, inventory, and promotion copies |
125	| `events.rs` | `RunEvent`, `RunEventBus`, `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel |
126	| `error.rs` | `DeadreckonError`, `Result<T>` |
127	
128	**`deadreckon-runtime` (`crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/lib.rs`).** The orchestration layer that depends on core, providers, and sandbox.
129	
130	| Module | Purpose |
131	|---|---|
132	| `turn_loop.rs` | `RunLoopConfig`, `RunLoopOutcome`, `run_turn_loop`, model action parsing, tool dispatch, cancellation, acceptance, and promotion |
133	| `polish.rs` | `polish_run_docs`, `PolishConfig`, skill resolution, polish input hashing, and nonfatal doc-provider polish |
134	
135	**`deadreckon-providers` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/lib.rs`).** A facade that re-exports the `Provider` trait, config types, HTTP adapter, smoke adapter, and router while keeping implementation modules private.
136	
137	| Module / file | Adapter |
138	|---|---|
139	| `http.rs` | `ProviderAdapter` (HTTP, used by `anthropic` / `openai` / `openai-compatible`) |
140	| `smoke.rs` | `ScriptedSmokeProvider` (`smoke`, dev-only, deterministic) |
141	| `router.rs` | `ProviderRouter` — config-driven fallback chain |
142	| `config.rs` | TOML config loading and built-in provider defaults |
143	| `types.rs` | public provider request/response/config traits and structs |
144	| `error.rs` | `ProviderError`, `Result<T>` |
145	| `cli_claude_code.rs` | `CliClaudeCodeProvider` — shells `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p` |
146	| `cli_codex.rs` | `CliCodexProvider` — shells `codex --ask-for-approval never exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox <mode>` |
147	| `cli_common.rs` | shared subprocess + allowlist machinery |
148	
149	**`deadreckon-sandbox` (`crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/lib.rs`).** A facade over sandbox backend resolution, command construction, policy, doctor checks, and subprocess supervision.
150	
151	| Module | Purpose |
152	|---|---|
153	| `backend.rs` | `SandboxBackend`, `SandboxError`, backend resolution |
154	| `spec.rs` | `SandboxSpec` |
155	| `commands.rs` | per-backend command/profile construction |
156	| `policy.rs` | `ToolSandboxPolicy` |
157	| `doctor.rs` | backend availability checks |
158	| `process.rs` | `run(SandboxSpec) -> SandboxRunOutput`, PID files, cancellation, SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation |
159	
160	**`deadreckon` (`crates/deadreckon/src/cli.rs`, `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs`, and `crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs`).** Clap parser definitions, command handlers, ratatui TUI for `attach`, and `dr-gate` as a standalone acceptance-marker writer.

175	### 2.4 Skills
176	
177	`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/default-coding/SKILL.md` is a single Markdown skill loaded at runtime. The skill is opaque to the binary; the run records `skill_name` + `skill_path` in `PipelineState` and includes the skill in the prompt frame. Skill swapping is in scope but only one skill ships today.
178	
179	### 2.5 External tools used at runtime
180	
181	| Tool | Caller | Purpose |
182	|---|---|---|
183	| `sandbox-exec` | `deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs` | macOS Seatbelt profile execution |
184	| `bwrap` | `deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs` | Linux Bubblewrap container |
185	| `docker` | `deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs` | Opt-in fallback |
186	| `claude` | `deadreckon-providers/src/cli_claude_code.rs:25` | CLI sub-agent provider |
187	| `codex` | `deadreckon-providers/src/cli_codex.rs:26` | CLI sub-agent provider |
188	| `cargo` | `deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:182,219,260` | Acceptance check for Rust targets |
189	| `sw_vers` / `uname` / `df` / `ps` | `deadreckon/src/main.rs:645,655,698,1362` | Doctor and PID liveness |
190	
191	Notably **not** shelled out: `asciinema`, `bollard`. (Demo cast is committed; Docker uses the `docker` CLI directly.)

194	
195	## 3. The Two-Layer Architecture
196	
197	deadreckon mirrors the Printing Press split (AS-BUILT §3):
198	
199	| Layer | Owns | Lives in | Language |
200	|---|---|---|---|
201	| **Skill** | Agent-facing prose, judgment, prompt frame | `skills/default-coding/SKILL.md` | Markdown |
202	| **Binary** | State, locks, sandboxes, providers, gates | `crates/deadreckon*` | Rust |
203	
204	The skill is invoked indirectly: it sits at the path recorded in `state.skill_path` and is read into the prompt frame by `build_prompt` in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`. The binary never reaches into skill internals. New skills can be added under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and selected with `deadreckon run --skill <name>`.
205	
206	This split lets each side do what it's good at:
207	
208	- The Rust binary enforces invariants — locks, atomic file ops, signed acceptance markers, sandboxed subprocesses.
209	- The Markdown skill makes judgment calls — what to ask the LLM for, what tool sequence to prefer, when to declare done.
210

213	## 4. State Machine & Persistence
214	
215	### 4.1 `PipelineState`
216	
217	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:77-110`:
218	
219	```rust
220	pub struct PipelineState {
221	    pub version: u32,                       // STATE_VERSION = 1 (line 15)
222	    pub goal: String,
223	    pub task_key: String,
224	    pub run_id: String,
225	    pub scope: String,
226	    pub status: RunStatus,
227	    pub current_phase_id: PhaseId,
228	    pub started_at: DateTime<Utc>,
229	    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
230	    pub cwd: PathBuf,
231	    pub run_root: PathBuf,
232	    pub working_dir: PathBuf,
233	    pub skill_name: String,
234	    pub skill_path: PathBuf,

481	## 7. Locks, Heartbeats, Crash Recovery
482	
483	### 7.1 `LockState`
484	
485	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/lock.rs:15-24`:
486	
487	```rust
488	pub struct LockState {
489	    pub task_key: String,
490	    pub run_id: String,
491	    pub scope: String,
492	    pub phase: String,
493	    pub pid: u32,
494	    pub acquired_at: DateTime<Utc>,
495	    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
496	}
497	```
498	
499	Lock file lives at `~/.deadreckon/locks/<scope>--<task_key>.lock` (`lock.rs:86`).
500	
501	### 7.2 Acquisition
502	
503	`lock.rs:89-158`:
504	
505	1. Create the `.lock` file.
506	2. `fs2::FileExt::try_lock_exclusive` for OS-level advisory lock.
507	3. If `EWOULDBLOCK`, read existing `LockState` from disk. If owner matches **or** lock is stale, proceed. Otherwise refuse.
508	4. Stale detection: `acquired_at` age > `DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER` (30 min, `lock.rs:13`) **or** `pid_is_alive(pid)` returns false. PID liveness is `nix::sys::signal::kill(pid, 0)` (`lock.rs:235-245`): `ESRCH` → dead, anything else → alive.
509	5. Write the new `LockState` to disk.
510	6. Return a `LockGuard` that releases on drop.
511	
512	### 7.3 Heartbeat
513	
514	`lock.rs:47-51`:
515	
516	```rust
517	pub fn heartbeat(&mut self, phase: impl Into<String>) -> Result<()> {
518	    self.state.phase = phase.into();
519	    self.state.updated_at = Utc::now();
520	    write_lock_state_to_file(&mut self.file, &self.path, &self.state)
521	}
522	```
523	
524	Updates `updated_at` to keep stale-detection at bay. Callers in the turn loop tag the current sub-phase (e.g., `"executing-turn-3"`).
525	
526	### 7.4 Release
527	
528	`lock.rs:53-76`. Drops the file lock, deletes the lock file, gracefully handles `NotFound`.
529	
530	### 7.5 Crash recovery
531	
532	If the process holding the lock dies, the lock file persists but `pid_is_alive(pid)` will return false. The next caller sees the stale state and reclaims it. The new caller writes its own PID; previous run state survives intact in `runstate/<scope>/runs/<dead_run_id>/`.

537	
538	### 8.1 `PromotionManifest`
539	
540	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs:14-23`:
541	
542	```rust
543	pub struct PromotionManifest {
544	    pub schema_version: u32,
545	    pub run_id: String,
546	    pub scope: String,
547	    pub goal: String,
548	    pub promoted_at: DateTime<Utc>,
549	    pub source_working_dir: PathBuf,
550	    pub provenance_hash: String,   // hash of provenance.jsonl bytes
551	}
552	```
553	
554	### 8.2 Promotion flow
555	
556	`promotion.rs:25-63`:
557	
558	1. **Guard.** `validate_acceptance_marker(state)?` — refuses if marker missing / wrong run_id / unsigned.
559	2. **Recovery.** `recover_promotion()` — idempotent if a previous attempt half-completed (§8.4).
560	3. **Idempotency check.** If `library/<scope>/<run_id>/manifest.json` already exists, update state and return — no work to do.
561	4. **Staging.** Create `library/<scope>/.{run_id}.promoting/` (parent dir created if needed).
562	5. **Move.** `fs::rename(working_dir, staging)` — atomic on same filesystem.
563	6. **Manifest.** Write `manifest.json` inside staging.
564	7. **Final rename.** `fs::rename(staging, library/<scope>/<run_id>/)` — atomic.
565	8. **State update.** `state.working_dir = library_dir`; `state.promoted_library_dir = Some(library_dir)`; `save_state()`.
566	
567	### 8.3 Where promotion happens
568	
569	In `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`, **before** `set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), Completed)`. If promotion fails, the run never reaches `Completed`. The `working/` directory is the source of truth until promotion; after promotion, the library copy is canonical and `working/` is gone.
570	
571	### 8.4 Crash recovery between rename steps
572	
573	`promotion.rs:65-84` handles the half-completed states:
574	
575	- If `staging` exists and final dir doesn't: complete the rename.
576	- If both exist: the final rename happened but didn't atomically remove staging; clean up staging.
577	- If final dir exists but its `manifest.json` is missing: write the manifest.
578	
579	This makes promotion crash-safe across a `kill -9` between the two renames.

704	
705	The loop does **not** retry on errors:
706	
707	- Provider error → propagates and the run fails.
708	- Tool-call non-zero exit → result fed back to history, next turn's prompt sees the failure; the model decides whether to retry.
709	- Acceptance failure → run fails; no auto-retry.

767	### 10.4 CLI sub-agent adapters
768	
769	**`cli:claude-code` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_claude_code.rs:1-127`).** Invocation:
770

772	claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p "<prompt>"
773	```

775	The `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag is non-negotiable (no human is in the loop). Stdout is captured to `request.output_path` (the turn's `claude.out`).

789	- `allow_network: true` (CLI agents need outbound for their own API calls).

791	**Spend (subscription).** Per `cli_claude_code.rs:100-110` and the equivalent in `cli_codex.rs`:

795	    cost_usd: 0.0,

818	for route in &self.routes {
819	    if !route.has_credential() { failures.push(...); continue; }
820	    match route.complete(request).await {
821	        Ok(resp) => return Ok(resp),
822	        Err(e) => failures.push(format!("{}: {e}", route.name())),
823	    }
824	}
825	Err(ProviderError::NoRoute(failures.join("; ")))
826	```

862	
863	`lib.rs:111-169` is the single dispatch entry point. It:
864	
865	1. Calls `build_command(spec)` to construct the per-backend invocation.

867	3. Persists the child PID to `spec.pid_file` (line 129) for `kill` supervision.
868	4. Reads stdout/stderr in parallel async tasks (`read_pipe`, lines 171–181).
869	5. Runs the cancellation `tokio::select!` (lines 131–151).

880	{network}                     ; (deny network*) unless allow_network=true
881	(allow file-read*

897	- `--tmpfs <cwd>/.deadreckon-home` and `--setenv HOME <cwd>/.deadreckon-home` (ephemeral tmpfs `$HOME`)

908

911	### 11.8 SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation
912	
913	`lib.rs:131-151`:
914	
915	```rust
916	if let Some(token) = spec.cancellation_token.as_ref() {
917	    tokio::select! {
918	        _ = token.cancelled() => {
919	            if let Some(pid) = pid {
920	                signal_pid(pid, false);                      // SIGTERM
921	                sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;         // 2s grace
922	                if child.try_wait()?.is_none() {
923	                    signal_pid(pid, true);                   // SIGKILL
924	                }
925	            }
926	            let _ = child.wait().await;
927	            if let Some(pid_file) = spec.pid_file.as_ref() {
928	                let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(pid_file).await;
929	            }
930	            return Err(SandboxError::Cancelled);
931	        }
932	        status = child.wait() => status
933	    }
934	}
935	```
936	
937	`signal_pid` is defined at `lib.rs:473-483` (uses `nix::sys::signal::kill`).

940	
941	## 12. Cancellation & Supervision
942	
943	### 12.1 Cancellation tokens
944	
945	The turn loop owns `run_token = CancellationToken::new()`; per turn it creates `turn_token = run_token.child_token()`; per tool call it can further create `tool_token = turn_token.child_token()`. The token threads through:
946	
947	- HTTP providers: `tokio::select!` on `token.cancelled()` vs the `reqwest` future.
948	- CLI providers: passed to `cli_common::run_cli` → `SandboxSpec.cancellation_token` → the sandbox layer.
949	- Tool dispatch (`Action::Bash`): passed to `run_sandbox(SandboxSpec { cancellation_token: Some(tool_token), ... })`.
950	
951	### 12.2 Child PID supervision
952	
953	Multiple sources contribute PIDs to track:
954	
955	- `state.child_pids: Vec<u32>` — populated by the CLI itself (`main.rs:333`).
956	- Per-subprocess PID files at `run_root/child-pids/*.pid` — written by the sandbox layer (`lib.rs:129`) and read by `supervised_pids()` (`main.rs:923`).
957	
958	`kill_command` (`main.rs:885-921`) reads both, releases the lock, sets `state.status = Killed`, and signals every PID via `terminate_pid(pid, force)`. Non-force: graceful (default signal), wait 1.5s, then SIGKILL anything still alive.
959	
960	### 12.3 What `kill` cannot do
961	
962	`kill` does **not** flip a cancellation token in a running deadreckon process. If a deadreckon `run` is still executing, `kill` only signals its child PIDs; the deadreckon process itself relies on its own cancellation token tree, which `kill` doesn't reach across processes. In practice this works because killing the children causes the providers/sandbox to error out, which the turn loop sees and propagates as a failure — but the seam is not as clean as it could be (this is named in the robustness rider as a hardening target).
963	
964	---
965	
966	## 13. Acceptance Gate & Anti-Self-Attestation
967	
968	### 13.1 The principle
969	
970	The agent (LLM) **cannot** be trusted to declare a run done. `Completed` is reachable only via an acceptance marker signed by an external binary that the agent does not have keys to.
971	
972	### 13.2 `AcceptanceMarker`
973	
974	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:16-28`:
975	
976	```rust
977	pub struct AcceptanceMarker {
978	    pub schema_version: u32,
979	    pub run_id: String,
980	    pub status: String,           // "pass" | "fail"
981	    pub produced_by: String,      // must be "dr-gate"
982	    pub checked_at: DateTime<Utc>,
983	    pub working_dir: PathBuf,
984	    pub signature: String,        // hash over fields + nonce
985	    pub check_count: usize,
986	}
987	```
988	
989	Marker location: `<run_root>/proofs/turn-acceptance.json`.
990	
991	### 13.3 `dr-gate` binary
992	
993	`crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs` (33 lines). Standalone binary that:
994	
995	1. Reads `--run <id>` and `--working-dir <path>`.
996	2. Loads `acceptance.yaml` (if present) from the run root.
997	3. Runs each check (cargo test, file-exists, content-match, build-success).
998	4. If all required checks pass, writes a signed `AcceptanceMarker` to `proofs/turn-acceptance.json`.
999	
1000	The marker's `signature` is computed from `gate/nonce` (a UUID written at run-init time by the deadreckon binary at `state.rs:188`). Only `dr-gate` reads the nonce; the agent never has access.
1001	
1002	### 13.4 Validation
1003	
1004	`gate.rs:88-118`:
1005	
1006	```rust
1007	pub fn validate_acceptance_marker(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<AcceptanceMarker> {
1008	    let path = marker_path(state);
1009	    let raw = std::fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
1010	    let marker: AcceptanceMarker = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(&path)?;
1011	    if marker.schema_version != 1 { return Err(...); }
1012	    if marker.run_id != state.run_id {
1013	        return Err("acceptance marker run_id ... does not match");
1014	    }
1015	    if marker.status != "pass" || marker.produced_by != "dr-gate" {
1016	        return Err("acceptance marker was not produced by dr-gate with pass status");
1017	    }
1018	    let expected = marker_signature(&state.run_root, &marker)?;
1019	    if marker.signature != expected {
1020	        return Err("acceptance marker signature is invalid; forged self-attestation refused");
1021	    }
1022	    Ok(marker)
1023	}
1024	```
1025	
1026	A forged marker by the agent fails the signature check at line 114.
1027	
1028	### 13.5 Where the gate is invoked
1029	
1030	The CLI sub-agent path and regular Done path in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` both call:
1031	
1032	```rust
1033	run_acceptance_gate(state)?;
1034	validate_acceptance_marker(state)?;
1035	promote_if_ready(state)?;
1036	```
1037	
1038	The first call invokes `dr-gate` as a subprocess. The second validates what `dr-gate` wrote. The third atomically swaps the working tree into the library.
1039	
1040	Failure at any step prevents the run from reaching `Completed`.

1110	## 15. Resume Semantics
1111	
1112	`crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:940-1000` is the `resume_command` handler.
1113	
1114	### 15.1 The Completed guard
1115	
1116	`main.rs:947`:
1117	
1118	```rust
1119	if state.status == RunStatus::Completed {
1120	    println!("run {} is already completed", state.run_id);
1121	    return Ok(());
1122	}
1123	```
1124	
1125	Completed runs cannot be resumed. They can be re-promoted (idempotent) but not re-entered into the loop. The only forward path for a completed run today is to start a new run.
1126	
1127	### 15.2 The replay process
1128	
1129	For non-Completed runs (`Failed`, `Killed`, `Paused`):
1130	
1131	1. Acquire the task lock.
1132	2. Clear `failure_reason`, `pause_reason`, `killed_at`.
1133	3. Set `status = Planned`.
1134	4. Optionally extend `max_wall_seconds` from the resume flag.
1135	5. Set `child_pids = vec![cli_pid]`.
1136	6. `save_state()`.
1137	7. Call `run_turn_loop` with `RunLoopConfig.from_turn = <CLI flag>`.
1138	8. The loop calls `load_or_reconstruct_history(state, from_turn)` in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`, which loads `history.json` if present, else reconstructs from `traces.jsonl`. With `from_turn = N`, history is truncated to N entries and `state.turn = N`.
1139	
1140	History reconstruction tolerates a `traces.jsonl` that ends mid-tool-call by ignoring incomplete entries — the next turn re-runs that turn.

1282	provider route and model before state is created; `run --model <model>` and
1283	`extend --model <model>` override one run; `deadreckon config provider
1284	<route>` and `deadreckon config model <model> --provider <route>` persist the
1285	defaults. CLI providers pass explicit model overrides through to the underlying

1289	### 19.2 BYOK posture
1290	
1291	Three credential paths:
1292	
1293	1. **HTTP key.** Set `api_key` directly or `api_key_env = "FOO"` to read at runtime.
1294	2. **CLI subscription.** Run with `--provider cli:claude-code` or `cli:codex`. The binary's presence in `$PATH` is the credential. No key required.
1295	3. **OpenAI-compatible.** Plug an OpenRouter or `llama.cpp` endpoint into `base_url` + `api_key`.
1296	
1297	`deadreckon init` (`main.rs:241-277`) walks the user through option (1) or (2): it detects `claude` and `codex` in `$PATH` and offers them as default providers before asking for keys.

1338	
1339	## 21. Key Design Decisions
1340	
1341	1. **No new `PipelineState` fields without a strong reason.** Parent lineage, materialization status, and other run-level metadata live in files inside the working tree (e.g., `.deadreckon/parent.json`), not on the state struct. This keeps `state.json` migration-safe.
1342	
1343	2. **Two-layer split is non-negotiable.** Skills (Markdown) own judgment; the binary owns invariants. A skill cannot bypass the gate; a gate cannot read prompts.
1344	
1345	3. **Anti-self-attestation via a nonce only `dr-gate` reads.** The agent can produce any output it wants; it cannot produce a valid `AcceptanceMarker.signature` because it never sees `gate/nonce`.
1346	
1347	4. **Atomic promotion before completion.** `Completed` is set only after the library swap succeeds. If promotion fails, the run fails. This means a `Completed` status always implies a durable artifact in `library/`.
1348	
1349	5. **Platform-native sandboxing.** No Docker daemon dependency. Seatbelt on macOS, bwrap on Linux. Docker is opt-in. The "running on host machine feels like a bad idea" pain point is solved without forcing Docker.
1350	
1351	6. **BYOK extends to subscriptions.** `cli:claude-code` and `cli:codex` are first-class providers, not afterthoughts. Most users will run deadreckon via subscription, not API keys.
1352	
1353	7. **Phase numbering with gaps (0, 10, 20, …).** Future phases can be inserted (e.g., a phase 15 for plan refinement) without rewriting durable state.
1354	
1355	8. **Append-only telemetry.** `spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, `events.jsonl` are immutable audit trails. The TUI and `show` command read them; nothing rewrites them.
1356	
1357	9. **The smoke provider is a real provider.** `--smoke` selects `ScriptedSmokeProvider`, which goes through the same `ProviderRouter::complete` path. There is no separate "smoke turn loop" — the loop is always the loop.
1358	
1359	10. **PID-aware locks with stale reclaim.** A crashed deadreckon process can be detected (its lock holder PID is dead via `kill(pid, 0)`); the next run reclaims the lock. No external lock daemon.
1360

1428	
1429	## 23. Glossary
1430	
1431	- **Run** — a single invocation of `deadreckon run <goal>`. Has a `run_id` (UUID), a `task_key` (slug + hash of goal), and a `scope` (slug + hash of repo path). Materialized in `~/.deadreckon/runstate/<scope>/runs/<run_id>/`.
1432	- **Scope** — `"<basename>-<fnv1a32-hex>"` of the canonical run-root path (git root or env var). Identifies a worktree.
1433	- **Task key** — `"<slug-of-goal>-<fnv1a32-hex>"`. Multiple runs of the same goal share a task key and a lock.
1434	- **Phase** — one of the seven gap-numbered stages of a run (`init`, `plan`, `provider`, `sandbox`, `execute`, `verify`, `complete`).
1435	- **Provider** — an implementation of the `Provider` trait that takes a prompt and returns text + spend. Can be HTTP (`anthropic`/`openai`/`openai-compatible`), CLI subprocess (`cli:claude-code`/`cli:codex`), or scripted (`smoke`).
1436	- **Action** — the JSON tag-typed enum the LLM emits per turn: `Bash`, `WriteFile`, `Done`. Parsed in the turn loop.
1437	- **Sandbox** — process-isolation backend selected at run start (`Auto` → platform-native by default; `SandboxExec` / `Bwrap` / `Docker` / `None`).
1438	- **Snapshot** — a full copy of `working/` taken before each turn. Lives at `snapshots/turn-<N>/`. Restored by `undo`.
1439	- **Promotion** — the atomic swap of `working/` into `library/<scope>/<run_id>/`. Only runs that pass the gate get promoted.
1440	- **Acceptance marker** — a signed JSON file (`proofs/turn-acceptance.json`) written by `dr-gate`. Its signature is tied to a per-run nonce only `dr-gate` reads.
1441	- **Spend** — a record of LLM cost per turn. USD for HTTP providers; wall-clock seconds + `subscription: true` for CLI providers.
1442	- **Provenance** — per-file attribution: which `tool_call_id` produced which file in which turn under which model.
1443

1445	
1446	## 24. Codebase Modes
1447	
1448	### 24.1 Why Codebase-Aware Running Is The Default
1449	
1450	The default `run` flow now gives the agent the user's project instead of an empty directory. This directly addresses the "agent never sees my repo" failure mode while preserving isolation: in git repos, deadreckon edits a new worktree and branch, not the user's checkout.
1451	
1452	### 24.2 Mode Resolution
1453	
1454	`run` resolves modes before state is written: `--fresh` keeps the old empty directory, `--in-place` requires explicit danger acknowledgement, `--worktree` forces git worktree mode, `--from <path>` forces copy mode, and a clean git repo defaults to worktree mode. Non-git interactive runs offer init/copy/cancel; non-interactive runs require an explicit mode or `--yes`.
1455	
1456	### 24.3 Worktree Mode
1457	
1458	Worktree mode creates branch `dr/<task-slug>-<run-id-prefix>` at `~/.deadreckon/worktrees/<scope>-<run-id-prefix>`. The branch is based on `--base` or the current branch. The source checkout is not touched until `deadreckon apply`.
1459	
1460	### 24.4 Copy Mode
1461	
1462	Copy mode seeds `runstate/<scope>/runs/<id>/working` from `--from <path>` using the `ignore` crate so `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, global gitignore, `.git`, `target`, and `node_modules` are not copied.
1463	
1464	### 24.5 In-Place Mode
1465	
1466	In-place mode sets `working_dir` to the source path and writes `.deadreckon/codebase.json` there. It requires `--in-place --i-know-its-a-lot` in non-interactive use. The user tree is edited directly; `undo` is the rollback tool.
1467	
1468	### 24.6 Fresh Mode
1469	
1470	Fresh mode is the previous empty-working-directory behavior behind `--fresh`. It records `mode: "fresh"` in `working/.deadreckon/codebase.json` and keeps existing smoke tests honest.
1471	
1472	### 24.7 `codebase.json`
1473	
1474	Mode metadata lives in `working/.deadreckon/codebase.json`, not `PipelineState`. Fields include `mode`, `source_path`, `source_git_root`, `branch_name`, `base_ref`, `base_sha`, `worktree_path`, dirty seeding flags, timestamp, and deadreckon version.
1475	
1476	### 24.8 Worktree Preflight
1477	
1478	Worktree preflight refuses non-git sources, repos with no commits, detached HEAD, mid-merge, mid-rebase, dirty trees unless `--allow-dirty`, branch collisions, and occupied worktree paths. Errors include `try:` lines.
1479	
1480	### 24.9 Preview Block
1481	
1482	Before file changes, `run` prints a single preview block with goal, source/git state, mode, branch/base/worktree when relevant, provider, sandbox, caps, and next verbs. `--preview` exits after printing; `--yes` skips confirmation.
1483	
1484	### 24.10 `apply` / `abandon`
1485	
1486	`apply` supports `squash` (default), `merge`, and `cherry-pick`. It refuses non-worktree runs and dirty user checkouts unless `--autostash` is set, then prints `git log -1 --stat`. `--cleanup` removes the temporary worktree/branch after successful apply. `abandon` / `discard` removes the worktree and branch when safe, supports `--keep-branch`, and writes `abandoned.json`.
1487	
1488	### 24.10.1 `status`, `list`, and `cleanup`
1489	
1490	`list` defaults to the current project scope so old runs from unrelated repos do
1491	not dominate the common path. `list --all` scans every scope; `show <run-id>`
1492	prints exact IDs, locations, docs, traces, and the next recommended action.
1493	`status` (alias `next`) prints the latest current-project run, its
1494	artifact/worktree locations, and the next recommended action. Running
1495	`deadreckon` with no subcommand dispatches to `status`.
1496	
1497	`cleanup` (alias `prune`) removes worktrees and temporary branches for already
1498	abandoned runs by default, with opt-in `--completed`, `--stale`, `--all`, and
1499	`--force` selectors. It leaves promoted library artifacts intact.
```

1518	## 25. Self-Documenting Runs
1519	
1520	### 25.1 The Three Artifacts
1521	
1522	Every run starts `working/.deadreckon/docs/` and writes three human-readable Markdown files:
1523	
1524	- `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` for the chronological implementation story.
1525	- `RUN-AS-BUILT.md` for the subsystem shape changed by the run.
1526	- `RUN-DECISIONS.md` for detected multi-alternative decisions.
1527	
1528	When the worktree has a nearby `AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md` or `AS-BUILT.md` and the diff is broad enough, deadreckon also emits `AS-BUILT-DELTA.md` as a proposed amendment.
1529	
1530	### 25.2 Frontmatter
1531	
1532	The docs use stoa-style bold frontmatter: Date, Last updated, Status, Run ID, Goal, optional Parent run, Commit span or working-directory mode, Owner, Provider, Sandbox, Spend, and Doc-writer. Fresh runs omit commit span; copy and in-place runs identify their working path.
1533	
1534	### 25.3 Per-Turn Templating
1535	
1536	After every successful tool/provider turn, `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` calls the turn-end documentation checkpoint. The deterministic record lands in `_incremental.jsonl`, rewrites the Markdown drafts, and emits a `docs_checkpoint` run event before the loop advances. This happens for both CLI sub-agent turns that complete in one provider process and JSON-action providers that may take many Bash/WriteFile/Done turns.
1537	
1538	Each turn record carries the full provider response capped at 50 KB, a short response summary, per-file add/delete counts, largest diff-hunk excerpts, binary markers, optional stdout/stderr samples, trace citation, snapshot reference, and worktree commit SHA when available.
1539	
1540	### 25.4 End-of-Run Polish Pass
1541	
1542	Before acceptance/promotion, `polish_run_docs` first writes deterministic docs, then optionally runs provider-backed polish unless `--no-docs` is set. The default path resolves four repo/user/project skills in order: `narrator-overview`, `narrator-phases`, `narrator-as-built`, and `narrator-decisions`. Each subcall receives the same run evidence plus a focused prompt, uses a 16K output-token budget by default, retries once on malformed JSON, and contributes to the merged docs.
1543	
1544	The legacy `run-narrator` single-call path remains available for custom installs that do not opt into split `doc_subskills`. Provider, JSON, or skill failures are nonfatal; templated docs remain and `polish.json` records `failed_subcall:<name>` when a split subcall failed.
1545	
1546	### 25.5 Phase And Decision Detection
1547	
1548	`docs.rs` coalesces turns into 3-8 phases by file overlap and tool-kind continuity. Decision candidates are detected with case-insensitive marker regexes and a minimum response length so incidental short phrases do not become decisions.
1549	
1550	### 25.6 Diff Coverage And Retry
1551	
1552	After polish, deadreckon verifies every changed file appears in `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` by relative path or basename. Missing files trigger up to two targeted `narrator-phases` retries with an explicit omission list; other subskills are not re-run for phase coverage misses. Remaining omissions are logged as `docs.warning` traces and do not fail the run.
1553	
1554	### 25.7 AS-BUILT-DELTA
1555	
1556	The delta is generated for worktree runs whose source has an AS-BUILT file at the root or beside touched files and whose diff touches at least three files or adds public/exported API. Public docs are copied to `working/docs/`; the branch gets a `turn docs: deadreckon run docs for <id>` commit so `apply` carries docs forward.
1557	
1558	### 25.8 Apply Commit Body
1559	
1560	When `deadreckon apply` builds the default squash or merge message, it reads `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` and `RUN-DECISIONS.md` to include an executive summary, phase list, decision count, open-thread count, and a `docs/RUN-NARRATIVE.md` trace pointer. `--message` still overrides the generated body.
1561	
1562	### 25.9 `deadreckon doc`
1563	
1564	`deadreckon doc <run-id>` prints the narrative by default. `--kind as-built|decisions|delta` selects another artifact, `--export <path>` writes it to disk, and `--force` overwrites exports or a prior polish result. `--polish` prints a preview listing provider, provider source, subskills, token budget, budget cap, and inputs hash before it calls the doc provider; `--no-confirm` skips the prompt for scripts. `--doc-provider <route>` overrides the automatic doc provider and `--budget-cap <usd>` limits the polish pass.
1565	
1566	### 25.10 Cost And Idempotency
1567	
1568	`polish.json` stores a SHA-256 inputs hash over goal, traces, provenance, spend, incremental records, changed files, and source AS-BUILT content. Schema v2 records `doc_provider_source`, `subcalls[]` with skill/status/provider/tokens/cost/duration/retries, `merged_at`, and `diff_coverage`. A matching polished hash skips duplicate provider calls unless forced. CLI subscription providers report wall time rather than USD cost, but the doc-provider resolver still records whether the route came from a flag, config, auto-detected subscription CLI, run provider fallback, or no provider.
1569	
1570	### 25.11 Skill Split Into Four Subskills
1571	
1572	The default polish path resolves `narrator-overview`, `narrator-phases`, `narrator-as-built`, and `narrator-decisions` separately so each prompt owns one documentation surface. The legacy `run-narrator` skill remains as the single-call compatibility path.
1573	
1574	### 25.12 Per-Turn Capture Richness
1575	
1576	Turn docs preserve the provider response up to 50 KB, stdout/stderr up to 10 KB each, per-file add/delete counts, binary markers, and the largest textual hunk excerpt. These fields are stored in `_incremental.jsonl` rather than `PipelineState`.
1577	
1578	### 25.13 Doc-Provider Auto-Resolution
1579	
1580	Doc polish chooses `--doc-provider`, then `[defaults].doc_provider`, then in-PATH subscription CLIs (`cli:codex`, `cli:claude-code`), then the run provider. If none resolve, the command fails with an actionable `try:` hint instead of silently leaving `Doc-writer: templated only`.
1581	
1582	### 25.14 Component Inference And Topology
1583	
1584	The deterministic as-built seed maps changed paths into concrete layers such as Rust crates, frontend components/routes, tests, documentation, manifests, migrations, and CI. Unmapped files are omitted instead of grouped under `Project files`; topology ASCII is emitted only when at least three top-level directories changed.
1585	
1586	### 25.15 Polish Preview And Budget Cap
1587	
1588	`deadreckon doc <id> --polish` estimates the maximum output-token cost before calling the provider. Paid API routes are refused when the estimate exceeds `--budget-cap` or `[defaults].doc_polish_budget_cap_usd`; subscription CLI routes estimate as `$0.00 (subscription)`.
1589	
1590	---
1591	
1592	## 28. Chains & Autonomous Goal Chaining
1593	
1594	### 28.1 Mental Model
1595	
1596	A chain is an ordered list of step goals plus branch, apply, budget, and stop policy. The conductor is a CLI process entered by `deadreckon chain ...` or `deadreckon chain run <id>`. It acquires a chain lock, spawns each step as a normal `deadreckon run --worktree`, waits for that run to complete and pass acceptance, applies it to the source branch when policy allows, then bases the next step on the updated head.
1597	
1598	Chain state is separate from `PipelineState`: no run schema fields were added. Files live under `~/.deadreckon/chains/<chain-id>/`.
1599	
1600	### 28.2 `chain.json`
1601	
1602	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/chain.rs` defines `Chain`, `ChainStep`, and `ConductorState`. The top-level chain records `chain_id`, `root_goal`, ordered `steps`, `branch_policy`, `apply_mode`, `apply_strategy`, `apply_allowlist`, `on_fail`, circuit-breaker counters, aggregate spend/wall caps, scope, base branch/SHA, cwd, provider/model/sandbox, status, pause/failure reason, conductor pid, timestamps, and deadreckon version.
1603	
1604	Each `ChainStep` records index, goal, status, run id, applied timestamp/SHA, failure reason, step cap, and actual spend. `ConductorState` is the live-process pointer in `conductor.json`: conductor pid, live step, live run id, and live child pid.
1605	
1606	### 28.3 Create And Run Shape
1607	
1608	The common path mirrors `run`:
1609	
1610	```bash
1611	deadreckon chain "step one" "step two" "step three" --yes
1612	deadreckon chain plan "build a chess app" --n 6 --yes
1613	```
1614	
1615	`chain expand` is an alias for `chain plan`. `--from-file` and `--from-stdin` accept newline-separated steps. `--draft` writes `chain.json` without starting the conductor. Bare `deadreckon chain` prints scoped status; `deadreckon chain run` resumes `latest`; `latest` and `last` are accepted anywhere a chain id is expected.
1616	
1617	### 28.4 Branch Policy
1618	
1619	`stack` bases step N+1 on the SHA applied by step N. `base` bases every step on the original chain base SHA. `merge` follows stack semantics but forces `apply --strategy merge`, producing merge commits instead of squash commits.
1620	
1621	### 28.5 Apply-Mode Green Policy
1622	
1623	`apply_mode=auto` advances only after the inner run completes, the acceptance marker validates, the target tree is clean, file changes match the allowlist when configured, and `on-promote` hooks accept the change. Failure pauses the chain and writes an actionable pause reason. `preview` and `manual` pause after the inner run so the user can inspect/apply explicitly.
1624	
1625	### 28.6 Conductor Lifecycle And Locks
1626	
1627	The conductor holds a `chain--<id>` lock while active. Inner runs keep their normal task locks. The conductor writes `conductor.json` before work starts and updates it while a child run is live. `chain kill` reads that file, kills the inner run through the normal cancel-marker path when a live run id exists, signals the child process, signals the conductor, waits briefly, then escalates.
1628	
1629	### 28.7 Hook Contract
1630	
1631	Hooks resolve in project, user, then repo order:
1632	
1633	```text
1634	.deadreckon/hooks/chain/<hook>
1635	~/.deadreckon/hooks/chain/<hook>
1636	/Users/gdc/deadreckon/hooks/chain/<hook>
1637	```
1638	
1639	Supported hooks are `pre-step`, `post-step`, `on-promote`, and `on-chain-end`. Payloads are JSON on stdin plus `DEADRECKON_CHAIN_ID`, `DEADRECKON_HOME`, and `DEADRECKON_STEP_INDEX`. Exit `0` proceeds. Exit `1` pauses or skips where defined. Exit `2` refuses/fails the transition. Every invocation appends `chain_hook_invoked`.
1640	
1641	### 28.8 Events And Promotion
1642	
1643	`chain-events.jsonl` is the chain audit log: created, step started, run completed, apply started, applied/refused, step failed, paused/resumed/killed/completed, undo, hooks, extend, and redo. `promotion.rs` also emits `RunPromoted { library_dir }`, so a chain can attach provenance to the promoted inner run artifact.
1644	
1645	### 28.9 Lifecycle Verbs
1646	
1647	`chain pause`, `resume`, `kill`, `undo`, `extend`, and `redo` compose with the existing run lifecycle. Undo reverts applied SHAs in reverse order. Extend inserts or appends a step and can reopen a completed chain when inserting. Redo chooses a specified step, the first failed step, or the latest applied step; applied-step redo requires `--reapply`, which reverts before requeueing.
1648	
1649	### 28.10 TUI Surfaces
1650	
1651	`chain attach <id>` opens a ratatui step timeline on TTYs and falls back to a plain snapshot off-TTY. The timeline shows policy, spend, step dots/statuses/run prefixes, recent chain activity, and controls for drill/show, redo, extend, pause, kill, detach, and scrolling. Single-run `attach` reads `.deadreckon/chain-step.json`, renders a chain context banner, and exposes `[c] Chain` to drill out to `chain attach`.
1652	
1653	### 28.11 Spend And Budgeting
1654	
1655	`--max-spend` is aggregate. Each pending step receives `(remaining cap)/(remaining pending steps)` as its inner run cap. The conductor reads the completed run's state and adds actual spend/wall time back into `chain.json`. `resume --max-spend-add` increases the aggregate ceiling; `--reset-breaker` clears the consecutive failure counter.
1656	
1657	### 28.12 Not Yet Built
1658	
1659	Out of scope for this alpha pass: mid-chain provider replanning, parallel/DAG steps inside one chain, cross-machine handoff, cloud sync, and a richer conflict-resolution UI. Those remain V1 candidates.
1660	
1661	- **Trace** — every LLM call and every tool dispatch, with latency + structured detail.
1662	- **CLI sub-agent** — a `cli:*` provider whose `complete()` invocation is one whole turn (the sub-agent does its own tool calls inside). Detected by `response.trace["kind"] == "cli_subagent"`.
1663	- **dr-gate** — the standalone binary at `crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs` that owns acceptance verification. The agent cannot impersonate it.
1664	- **BYOK** — Bring Your Own Key. In deadreckon this extends to subscriptions: a Claude Max or ChatGPT Pro user can drive deadreckon via `cli:*` providers without an API key.
1665	
1666	---
1667	
1668	*This document is canonical for the alpha-tier reality of deadreckon. Future hardening passes (per the robustness rider) and feature passes (per the usability rider) will update sections 6, 9, 11, 13, 14, 18, and 22 in particular. Last regenerated by an agent team from a deep code map; cross-check against the current code before relying on any specific line number.*
1669

+        (Ok(left), Ok(right)) => left == right,
+        _ => false,
+    }

- **§25.4 Self-Documenting Runs** — recorded that `--smoke` now implies `effective_no_docs` unless `--doc-provider` is set, and that `print_status_card` surfaces a polish-failed detail line.
- **§22 What's Built** — added bullets for shell completions, streaming acceptance progress, extend/resume startup parity, and acceptance-spec carry-forward.
